deal.activate_success: Work started! Deadline is now running.
deal.funded_executor_hint: Deal is funded and waiting for you. Click Start Work — the deadline timer begins then. If you don't start within {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}, the client can request a refund.
deal.funded_client_hint: The executor needs to confirm they're starting. If they don't start within {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}, you can trigger a refund.
deal.active_executor_hint: Complete the work and click Mark Done when ready. The client will review and release payment.
deal.active_client_hint: The executor is working on your task. When they mark it done, review and release payment — or raise a dispute if needed.
deal.refund_success: Dispute resolved · Budget refunded to client.
deal.pay_executor_success: Dispute resolved · Funds paid to executor.
deal.chat_desc: Encrypted private messages with your counterparty
deal.closed_hint: This deal is closed. No further actions required.
deal.dispute_active_hint: Arbitrator has been notified. Chat with them to resolve.
deal.fund_dispute_btn: Pay {amount} USDC to get an arbiter
deal.fund_dispute_hint: Small disputes rarely attract an arbiter — the fee on this deal pays them too little. Topping it up makes the case worth taking. If nobody takes it anyway, the {amount} USDC comes back to you — sent automatically, or waiting on this page to withdraw.
deal.fund_dispute_success: Paid · an arbiter now has a reason to take this case.
deal.fund_dispute_funded: An arbiter has been paid for on this dispute. If nobody takes it, the money comes back — sent automatically, or waiting on this page to withdraw.
deal.refund_bounty_hint: A dispute you paid an arbiter for ended without a verdict, or the verdict was overturned. The money is yours — it just isn't sent back on its own.
deal.refund_bounty_success: Withdrawn · the top-up is back in your wallet.
deal.dispute_arbiter_topup_notice: That ending can be avoided: while the dispute is open, the deal page lets either side top up the arbiter's pay — that is what makes a small case worth taking. The option only shows up when the fee alone is too small; on a larger deal there is nothing to add. If nobody takes the case even after a top-up, it comes back — sent automatically, or waiting on the deal page to withdraw.
deal.dispute_reason_hint: Describe the issue clearly — if an arbiter takes the case, this is the first thing they read.
deal.dispute_fee_notice: Arbitration costs {fee} USDC out of the {pot} USDC in escrow — charged either way, whoever turns out to be right.
deal.dispute_no_arbiter_notice: If no arbiter takes the case within {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} and both sides answered it, the escrow is split — {toExecutor} USDC to the executor, {toClient} USDC to the client. Nobody judged, so nobody wins. A side that never answers gets a quarter instead of half.
deal.dispute_terms_unreadable: Couldn't read this deal's arbitration terms — how the escrow would be settled is unknown right now. Try again in a moment.
deal.dispute_reason_placeholder: e.g. Executor stopped responding after receiving the brief. Deadline passed with no deliverable submitted.
deal.dispute_respond_success: Answered · your side is on the record.
deal.dispute_respond_prompt: Answer this dispute before {date}. If you stay silent and no arbiter takes the case, you get a quarter of the escrow instead of half.
deal.dispute_respond_done: You answered this dispute. If no arbiter takes it, the escrow is split in half.
deal.dispute_respond_done_waiting: You answered this dispute. The other side hasn't answered yet — if it stays silent and no arbiter takes the case, you get three quarters of the escrow.
deal.timeout_activation_success: Executor timed out · Budget refunded to you.
deal.timeout_deadline_success: Deadline passed · Budget refunded to you.
deal.timeout_arbiter_success: Arbiter timed out · Budget refunded to client.
deal.timeout_arbiter_split_success: Nobody took the dispute · {toExecutor} USDC to the executor, {toClient} USDC to the client.
deal.timeout_arbiter_unknown_success: Dispute closed · check your wallet to see what actually arrived.
deal.timeout_arbiter_unanswered_success: Dispute closed · {toExecutor} USDC to the executor, {toClient} USDC to the client. The side that never answered got a quarter.
deal.arbiter_trust: Protected by {count, plural, one {# independent arbiter} other {# independent arbiters}} — a dispute is judged on-chain by whoever takes the case. If nobody takes it in time, the escrow is split instead of judged.
deal.arbiter_trust_generic: Dispute resolution is handled on-chain by registered arbiters.
deal.stale_activation_body: The activation window has passed. Either party can trigger a refund — funds will return to the client automatically.
deal.stale_deadline_body: The work deadline has expired with no delivery. Either party can trigger a refund to close this deal.
deal.stale_autorelease_body: Work was marked done and the client didn't review in time. Either party can trigger automatic payment to the executor.
deal.stale_arbiter_body: No arbiter resolved this dispute in time. Either party can trigger an automatic refund to the client.
deal.stale_arbiter_split_body: Nobody took this dispute within {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}, and both sides answered it. Either party can close it now — the escrow is split: {toExecutor} USDC to the executor, {toClient} USDC to the client. Nobody judged, so nobody wins.
deal.stale_arbiter_unanswered_body: Nobody took this dispute within {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}, and one side never answered it. Either party can close it now — the escrow goes {toExecutor} USDC to the executor and {toClient} USDC to the client. Staying silent costs a quarter of the escrow.
deal.receipt_hint: A permanent on-chain NFT record of this deal. Non-transferable — yours to keep.

chat.title: Messages
chat.encrypted: Encrypted · only you hold the keys
chat.paste_address_hint: Paste a wallet address to start chatting
chat.preview_unreadable: This message can’t be read on this device
chat.start_hint: Start a chat from a deal or use the + button above
chat.empty_state_hint: Choose from the list or start a new chat
chat.wallet_required: Connect your wallet to view your conversations
chat.share_invite_hint: Share your chat link — when they open it and connect, messaging activates.
chat.list_stale: This list may be out of date. Refresh
chat.attach_file_title: Attach file (encrypted, kept 7 days, longer while the deal is open, max {mb} MB)
chat.files_deal_only: Files available only in active deals
chat.e2e_notice: Encrypted · kept 7 days, longer while the deal is open · only the two of you hold the key
chat.stream_dead: Connection lost — new messages not arriving
chat.messaging_off_hint: Turn on messaging to read and send messages here.
chat.messaging_off_same_key: An ordinary wallet only needs a signature: the key is derived from it, so the same key comes back and your old messages open.
chat.restore_who_for: The code is only for smart-contract wallets (Safe, Coinbase Smart Wallet), whose key is random. An ordinary wallet needs no code.
chat.file_expired: Storage period ended — ask for the file again
chat.no_access: Access not confirmed — reopen the chat and try again
chat.recovery_warning_access: This is access to all your messages. Anyone who gets these 12 words can read everything. They cannot be revoked or changed.
chat.recovery_warning_loss: Lose them and your messages are gone for good.
chat.privacy_badge_storage: Messages are encrypted. The server keeps them unreadable and holds no keys.
chat.privacy_badge_dispute: In a dispute, either side can present the conversation to an arbiter — from their own device.
chat.chain_gap: A message is missing here — it never arrived, or it was not handed over
chat.chain_gap_start: The beginning of this conversation was not presented
chat.pass_signature_hint: Your wallet is asking for a signature: it proves to the server that these bags are yours. Normally it repeats at most once every 12 hours; if your browser blocks storage (private mode), once per tab load. It never touches your chat key.
chat.signature_wanted: Confirm the signature in your wallet
chat.signature_wanted_pass: It proves to the server that these bags are yours. Your conversation is already open — the signature is only needed to fetch new messages.
chat.signature_wanted_key: Your chat key is derived from it: once per device, silently after that.
chat.signature_wanted_where: The prompt may have opened in your wallet app — check there.
chat.wallet_not_answering: The wallet isn’t answering. If no signature prompt appeared, reconnect the wallet from the header menu.
chat.key_not_saved: The chat key could not be saved on this device — messaging works, but only until you reload the tab.
chat.key_not_saved_blocked: The chat key was not saved: the site is open in another tab. Close it, or you will be asked to sign every time.
chat.chain_unverified: Some of your peer’s messages failed the authenticity check and are not shown.
chat.undecryptable: Some messages cannot be opened with your key — they may be sealed to an older one.
chat.recovery_warning_keep: Write them down and keep them secret.
chat.recovery_skip: Skip, I will write it down later
chat.recovery_where: The code stays in the wallet menu under “Recovery code” for as long as chat is on for this device.
chat.recovery_check_title: Let us check you wrote it down
chat.recovery_check_hint: Type in three words by their numbers.
chat.messages_not_sent: Some of your messages never left this device. Your contact sees a gap where they should have been.
chat.numbering_reset: This device started numbering the conversation over. Your contact may see a gap — it is not their doing, and not a forgery.
chat.restore_hint: Type or paste the twelve words of your recovery code.
chat.restore_err_empty: Enter the twelve words of the code.
chat.restore_err_word_count: There must be exactly twelve words.
chat.restore_err_unknown_word: Word {n} is misspelled — there is no such word in the list.
chat.restore_err_checksum: The words do not add up. Check the spelling and the order.
chat.restore_err_busy: This device already has a chat for this wallet. To replace it, forget the current one first — its key will be removed from the device.
chat.restore_err_not_applicable: For this wallet the recovery is the wallet itself: sign the same data with it and the chat key comes back on its own. A recovery code is not needed.
chat.restore_err_storage_read: Could not read the device storage. We do not know whether a key is there, and we are not touching it.
chat.restore_err_storage_slow: Device storage is not responding. Close other tabs of this site and try again.
chat.restore_err_signature: The wallet did not sign the request.
chat.disable_eoa: The chat key will be removed from this device. To come back, sign the same data with the same wallet — your messages stay.
chat.disable_contract: The chat key will be removed from this device. For this wallet the key is random and there is no second source: without the recovery code your messages are gone for good.
chat.file_too_large: File is too large. The limit is {mb} MB.
chat.key_not_saved_contract: The chat key did not save on this device. For this wallet the key is random: after a reload a new one is created and the old messages will not open. Write down your recovery code now.
chat.off_version_unknown: This device holds a record of an unfamiliar version — the app looks older than it. We are leaving it alone so your key is not lost. Reload the page later.
chat.off_unknown: Something got in the way of opening your messages. Try again.
chat.bags_pending: Still picking up messages from storage: {n}.
chat.bags_failed: Some messages could not be picked up from storage. They are not lost — try reconnecting.
chat.push_no_pass: Notification not sent: there is no chat session on this device.
chat.push_rate_limited: Notifications are going out too often — this one was skipped. Wait a moment.
chat.push_error: The notification could not be sent. Your message was delivered, but the other person will not see it until they open the chat.
chat.key_unannounced_title: No one can message you yet
chat.key_unannounced_body: Your key is created, but nobody knows about it yet.
chat.key_unannounced_call: Confirm in your wallet — and people will find you.
chat.key_elsewhere_title: Your chat is already on another device
chat.key_elsewhere_switch_note: Earlier conversations will not open here.
chat.present_pick_hint: Tick the messages the arbiter should see. Everything you tick goes to them in full.
chat.present_pick_fits_unknown: That much does not fit into one bag. Untick some messages — we could not work out how many would fit.
chat.present_warn_title: This goes to the arbiter and cannot be taken back
chat.present_warn_turn: This is arbiter number {n} on this dispute.
chat.present_warn_turn_unknown: How many arbiters have handled this dispute — we could not work out.
chat.present_warn_everything: Everything inside the ticked messages goes out in full: the text, and the names of the files mentioned in it — including anything about third parties who are not in this dispute.
chat.present_warn_files: The file itself will not reach the arbiter: its name, size and type will. There is no way to show them the file — not even for you.
chat.present_warn_final: It cannot be taken back: what is sent is already with the arbiter.
chat.present_consent: I understand: this goes to the arbiter, and it cannot be taken back
chat.present_not_anchored: The arbiter has the messages. This is not marked on chain: the time of the presentation is fixed nowhere.
chat.present_anchor_failed: Marking on chain did not work. The arbiter has the messages — try again later.
chat.present_anchor_no_wallet: Your wallet or the node is not answering — there is nothing to mark on chain with right now. The arbiter still has the messages.
chat.present_fetch_unknown: Whether it was picked up could not be checked
chat.present_draft_found: Earlier you put together {n} message(s) and did not send them. The ticks can be brought back — the presentation is then built again, for the arbiter who is on the dispute now.
chat.present_draft_sent: You have already presented this: {n} message(s). The same bag cannot be forwarded — it is sealed for that arbiter. The ticks can be brought back, and the presentation is built again, for the arbiter who is on the dispute now.
chat.present_err_arbiter_has_no_key: The arbiter has not published a chat key on chain — there is nobody to seal this for yet.
chat.present_err_peer_has_no_key: The other side has no chat key: a presentation is sealed for both of you, and theirs is missing.
chat.present_err_too_large: This does not fit into one bag — untick some messages.
chat.present_err_no_session: Your chat keys are not confirmed on this device, so there is nothing to sign this with.
chat.present_err_attestation_missing: Your chat keys are not certified. Press "certify keys" — your wallet will ask for a signature.
chat.present_err_attestation_expired: The certificate of your chat keys is over a year old. Certify them again — your wallet will ask for a signature.
chat.present_err_attestation_unproven: There is nothing to check the certificate against: the chain did not answer, or this wallet has no code on chain yet. Signing again will not help — see to the network.
chat.present_err_not_disputed: Nobody is handling this dispute right now — there is no arbiter to present it to.
chat.present_err_arbiter_changed: The arbiter changed while you were deciding. Build it again: the previous arbiter's key will not open for the new one.
chat.present_err_key_changed: The arbiter turned over their chat key while you were deciding. Build it again: the previous key will no longer open for them.
chat.present_err_arbiter_left: Nobody is on this dispute right now. There is nobody to present it to — wait for an arbiter.
chat.present_err_busy: Already sending — wait for it to finish.
chat.present_err_chain_unavailable: The chain did not answer, so who is on the dispute could not be checked. Nothing was sent — try again.
chat.present_err_not_a_party: The dispute box takes bags only from the two sides of the deal. Nothing was sent.
chat.present_err_no_such_deal: The server does not know this deal. Nothing was sent.
chat.present_err_rate_limited: Too often. Nothing was sent — wait a minute.
chat.present_err_box_refused: The dispute box did not accept it. Nothing was sent.
chat.present_err_offline: Could not reach the server. Nothing was sent.
chat.present_err_pass_refused: The server did not accept the pass. Nothing was sent.
chat.present_draft_not_saved: Sent, but it could not be written down on this device: after a reload the page will remember neither "placed" nor the ticks. The bag is in the box — that is the server's answer, not our record.
chat.present_err_internal_error: Something broke on this device and the presentation was not put together. Nothing was sent.
chat.present_pick_legacy_mark: the arbiter will be able to open the attachment of this message
chat.present_warn_legacy_files: Exception, and it matters: {n} of the ticked messages carry the attachment key inside the message itself. The arbiter will be able to open those files.

notifications.empty_hint: Notifications about your deals, jobs, and services will appear here
notifications.push_blocked: Push notifications are blocked by your browser. Go to browser settings → Site permissions to re-enable.
notifications.push_enable_failed: Failed to enable push notifications. Check your browser settings or try again later.
notifications.push_stale: Push notifications may have stopped arriving — this device's registration is over a day old. Turn them on again to refresh it.

arbiter.title: Arbiter Hub
arbiter.subtitle: Review disputed deals, claim cases, and resolve them.
arbiter.presentations_desc: What the parties have presented to YOU in this dispute. Only bags sealed to your on-chain key can be opened — that is the whole guarantee.
arbiter.presentations_no_cases: You have not taken on a dispute yet. A presentment box belongs to whoever is handling the dispute — it opens for you once you claim one.
arbiter.presentations_box_unreadable: The box could not be read. This does NOT mean it is empty — try again in a minute.
arbiter.presentations_err_not_mine_now: This dispute is not yours to read any more — it was reclaimed while you were reading. The box is intact; whoever handles the dispute now can open it.
arbiter.presentations_err_no_such_deal: Our server does not know this deal address. Nothing was read and nothing was lost — but the box, if any, is not here.
arbiter.presentations_err_chain_unavailable: The chain did not answer, so the server could not check who is handling this dispute. This says nothing about what is in the box — try again in a minute.
arbiter.presentations_err_too_often: Too many reads in one minute. The server counts this box and your chat separately, but this browser keeps ONE read budget for both — so a busy chat can hold the box up too. Everything is still there; come back in a minute.
arbiter.presentations_err_pass_stale: Your storage pass has expired. Press again — your wallet will sign a new one.
arbiter.presentations_key_needed: This device has no chat key yet. Presentments are sealed to your key, so opening them needs one wallet signature.
arbiter.presentations_empty: Nothing has been presented to you here yet. That does not mean a party stayed silent — ask them in chat.
arbiter.presentations_index_rebuilt: Our server rebuilt its bag listing, so presentments may be missing from this view. An empty box here is NOT proof that a party stayed silent. Ask them in chat, and open the box again in a few minutes.
arbiter.presentations_partial_budget: Read {read} of {total}. The read budget ran out — this browser keeps ONE read budget for the box and your chat together. The rest is still there; come back in a minute.
arbiter.presentations_partial_transport: Read {read} of {total}, then the connection to our server broke. The rest is still there, but we cannot say when it will be readable — try again, and if it keeps breaking, the trouble is not in the box.
arbiter.presentations_partial_unread: Read {read} of {total}. The rest was not read at all — the reasons are listed above. This is not the read budget: nothing was spent on those.
arbiter.presentations_sealed_for_others: {count} bag(s) are marked for a different arbiter. That is our SERVER's word, not a chain fact — you cannot open them. Ask the party to present again.
arbiter.presentations_not_ours: {count} bag(s) here did not open with your key. That is what we COUNTED, not what anyone claimed — so the box is not empty, it is unreadable to you. Ask the party to present again.
arbiter.presentations_not_ours_fetched: {count} of those had already been picked up before this reading. The listing does not record by whom — it may have been the previous arbiter, or you on an earlier visit. The mark is about bytes leaving the server, not about anyone reading them.
arbiter.presentations_not_parsed: {count} bag(s) never got as far as a verdict: not a presentment in a shape we know (a party's client may be a different version), gone from storage, too large, or filed under another box. The box is NOT empty — ask the party to present again.
arbiter.presentations_not_mine: This dispute is handled by {arbiter}, not you — that is what our SERVER last read from the chain, not a live answer. The box is closed for you. If you have only just claimed this dispute, open the box again in a little while.
arbiter.presentations_box_closed: Nobody is handling this dispute, so the box is closed. Whatever is inside stays sealed to the keys it was sealed to. This too is our server's last reading of the chain, not a live answer — if you have only just claimed the dispute, open the box again in a little while.
arbiter.presentations_turn_known: Arbiters before you in this dispute: {count}
arbiter.presentations_turn_unknown: How many arbiters handled this dispute before you — could not be read from the chain. That is not "none".
arbiter.presentations_device_key_differs: The chat key on this device differs from the one recorded on-chain. Presentments are sealed to the on-chain key and will not open here.
arbiter.presentations_device_key_chain_missing: You have no chat key recorded on-chain. Presentments are sealed to the ON-CHAIN key, so there is nothing a party could seal to you — an empty box here says nothing about anyone staying silent. Publish your key on the «My Cases» tab.
arbiter.presentations_device_key_chain_unread: We could not read your on-chain key, so there is nothing to compare this device's key against. If presentments do not open, the cause may be here rather than in a party's silence.
arbiter.presentation_counts_declared: Party's own count: shown {read}, hidden {hidden}, not prepared {notPrepared}
arbiter.presentation_counts_measured: Counted while reading: opened {read}, would not open {unopened}, hidden {hidden}, not prepared {notPrepared}
arbiter.presentation_anchor_match: The digest matches the record on chain — block {block}.
arbiter.presentation_anchor_match_no_block: The digest matches the record on chain. No block number: the event feed looks back one day, and this record is older.
arbiter.presentation_anchor_mismatch: DOES NOT MATCH. Digests recorded on chain for this deal: {count}, and none matches the bytes of this bag. So this is not what was presented: the bytes were swapped, or the bag was rebuilt after the record.
arbiter.presentation_anchor_absent: Not recorded on chain. That is not a flaw in the presentment: the party may not have reached the second step. There is simply nothing to order this bag by.
arbiter.presentation_anchor_unread: The chain did not answer about digests — there is nothing to check against. This is NOT «not recorded».
arbiter.presentation_anchor_dupes: The same digest is recorded on chain {count} times — a repeat of «record» after a dropped reply. This is not a forgery.
arbiter.presentation_anchor_order_digest_first: The presentment went on chain first: digest — block {digest}, the arbiter’s «asked, no reply» record — block {record}.
arbiter.presentation_anchor_order_record_first: The arbiter’s «asked, no reply» record went first: block {record}, the presentment digest — block {digest}.
arbiter.presentation_anchor_order_out_of_window: There is nothing to order by: the feed search does not reach back to the start of the dispute. Whether an arbiter record exists earlier, we do not know. This is NOT «there is no record» — ask for a review if the order matters.
arbiter.presentations_anchor_window: The feed search covered blocks {from}–{to}. Anything earlier did not make it into the ordering — that is the limit of the search, not an empty chain.
arbiter.presentations_anchor_truncated: The chain holds more digests than we read: {count} taken. A non-match could simply mean we did not finish reading — which is why it is called «unknown».
arbiter.presentation_anchor_order_same: The digest and the arbiter’s «asked, no reply» record landed in the same block — {block}.
arbiter.presentations_no_response_record: The chain holds an arbiter’s «asked for the chat, no reply» record: block {block}, {count} such records in total.
arbiter.presentation_counts_disagree: The party's count does not match what was counted here. A broken chain can cause this too — trust the counted one.
arbiter.presentation_bad_signature: The presentment signature does not check out: who assembled it is unknown, so no content is shown. The per-message verdicts below are real — they are computed from the bytes themselves.
arbiter.presentation_malformed: This is not a presentment: wrong shape.
arbiter.msg_frame_broken: Message bytes do not check out: {reason}
arbiter.msg_file_fact: Attachment: {name}, {size} bytes, type {mime} — named only, the file itself is not sent to you at all.
arbiter.msg_legacy_key_exposed: This attachment's key was left in the message in the clear (old format).
arbiter.msg_author_attested: Signed with a key its owner attested on {date} (UTC). An attestation cannot be revoked: if the device was stolen after that date, a thief signs with the very same key and this line looks exactly the same.
arbiter.disputes_desc: All active disputes — claim a case to become its arbiter, then chat with both parties and resolve.
arbiter.my_cases_desc: Disputes you have claimed. Submit a verdict within {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} of the dispute being raised — after that the case closes without you and counts as a no-show.
arbiter.no_cases: You haven't claimed any disputes yet
arbiter.history_desc: All disputes you arbitrated — resolved, refunded, or completed.
arbiter.search_placeholder: Search by deal, client or executor address…
arbiter.chief_desc: You are the chief arbiter — you can add and remove arbiters.
arbiter.claim_hint: Claim this case to join the deal chat and contact both parties.
arbiter.claim_success: Dispute claimed. You are now the arbiter.
arbiter.claim_press_again: Press again — the page went to your wallet
arbiter.key_directory_mismatch: Note: our server has a different chat key on file for you than the one recorded on-chain. We're using the on-chain key — it's the one that decides.
arbiter.no_key_notice: Your chat key for this case isn't recorded on-chain yet — that's what correspondence will be sealed to, once case presentment ships. Publishing it is one transaction.
arbiter.no_key_notice_demoted: You're no longer a registered arbiter, so a chat key can't be published for this case — nothing can be sealed to you, and this isn't something you can fix yourself.
arbiter.key_published: Done — your key is recorded on-chain now, ready for when case presentment ships.
arbiter.release_success: Claim released. Deal is open for other arbiters.
arbiter.resolve_hint: Chat with both parties above to understand the situation, then make your ruling.
arbiter.dispute_log_sign_timeout: Signing took too long — the request expired. Try again.
arbiter.no_history_log: The platform keeps no log — the parties present the conversation themselves
arbiter.window_expired: Window expired — parties can trigger refund
arbiter.resolve_client_desc: Refund Client — client gets their USDC back (executor did not deliver).
arbiter.resolve_executor_desc: Pay Executor — executor gets paid (work was done).
arbiter.role_unreadable: Couldn't check your arbiter role — the network didn't answer. You haven't lost access; the check simply didn't go through.
arbiter.no_response_hint: Only the fact and the time go on-chain: no XP, no reputation, no weight in the verdict. It can be recorded once.
arbiter.no_response_wait_dh: You can record this in {d}d {h}h — earlier the chain refuses.
arbiter.no_response_wait_hm: You can record this in {h}h {m}m — earlier the chain refuses.
arbiter.no_response_wait_m: You can record this in {m}m — earlier the chain refuses.
arbiter.no_response_recorded: Recorded {at}: asked for the conversation, no response. It cannot be recorded a second time.
arbiter.no_response_claim_unknown: You took this dispute before the chain started remembering when a dispute is taken — there is nothing to count the delay from.
arbiter.no_response_release_open: The dispute window is still open: release the dispute and take it again — the countdown starts from that moment.
arbiter.no_response_release_closed: The dispute window has already closed: you cannot release and take it again, so silence cannot be recorded for this dispute at all.
arbiter.no_response_release_verdict: A verdict on this dispute has already been submitted: the dispute cannot be released, so silence cannot be recorded for it.
arbiter.no_response_release_unknown: Whether the dispute window is still open we cannot say: the chain did not answer. While it is open, the only way out is to release the dispute and take it again.
arbiter.no_response_not_mine: Only whoever handles the dispute right now can record «no response» — on-chain that is {arbiter}.
arbiter.no_response_not_claimed: Nobody handles this dispute right now: there is no claim on-chain. The «no response» record belongs to whoever handles the dispute, which is why it is not here.
arbiter.no_response_chain_unread: The chain has not answered yet whether «no response» can be recorded. The button is absent on purpose: promising what the chain has not confirmed is worse than waiting.
arbiter.no_response_done: Recorded on-chain: asked for the conversation, no response.

onboarding.title: How Hexseal works
onboarding.subtitle: Decentralized freelance on Base — no middlemen, code enforces.
onboarding.step1_desc: Clients post jobs on the Job Board. Executors list services. Browse and respond to offers.
onboarding.step2_desc: Both parties agree to terms. A smart contract is deployed — this is your binding agreement.
onboarding.step3_desc: Client deposits USDC into the contract. Funds are locked on-chain — no one can touch them until conditions are met.
onboarding.step4_desc: Executor marks done. Client releases payment. No release after timeout? Funds auto-approve. Dispute? Arbiter resolves.
onboarding.step5_desc: You sign transactions, the platform pays gas. No ETH needed — just USDC for deal funding.
onboarding.final_desc: Go straight to where you need to be.

hints.board_apply: Tap a card to expand it and apply — the client will review your request.
hints.deal_fund_client: Fund the escrow to lock your payment on-chain and kick off the deal. The executor can't touch the funds until they deliver.
hints.deal_activate_executor: Activate to confirm you've started work. This starts the deadline clock.
hints.deal_markdone_executor: Mark done when you've delivered. The client then has a window to review — after that it auto-releases.
hints.deal_release_client: The executor marked the work done. Review it and release funds when you're satisfied.
hints.executor_board_request: Tap a service card to expand it and send a hire request — set your budget and terms, the executor will confirm.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.subtitle: Frequently asked questions about Hexseal — the decentralized freelance protocol on Base.
faq.a_what_is: Hexseal is a decentralized freelance marketplace on Base. Clients post jobs, executors submit work, and funds are locked in an on-chain escrow contract — enforced by code, not by a platform admin.
faq.a_who_controls: The deal's own contract. USDC inside an Agreement can leave it only along paths written into that contract: the client releases it, the auto-approve timeout releases it, a refund returns it, or an arbiter's verdict settles it. Only the client or the executor can raise a dispute, and the only recipients any path can pay are the two parties and the protocol's arbitration fee — the Agreement's code is fixed when the deal is created. One human lever remains, and we would rather name it than have you find it: the Diamond owner can replace protocol code, and until a verdict is final that key can overturn or freeze it, which decides who receives a disputed escrow. Why it is like this today: everything runs on testnet with test USDC and without an external audit, and at that stage one key means a money bug is fixed the same day. The plan — a plan, not something the code enforces yet — is to hand governance to a multisig at the mainnet launch, where real money appears. Until then, “autonomous” describes this protocol's logic, not its governance.
faq.a_is_free: Transactions are gasless — the platform relayer pays the ETH gas on your behalf, so you never need ETH. The platform fee is a different matter: it is charged in USDC on top of the deal amount, never taken out of it, and it is charged up front — when a job is posted, when a service is listed, and when a client sends a request for a listed service — never on completion. A client posting a job pays the escrowed amount plus the fee; requesting a listed service works the same way. An executor listing a service pays the fee alone, since there is no deal amount yet to base it on — that fee is a flat amount, not a percentage. Everywhere else, the fee is a percentage of the deal amount with a floor minimum. Only that floor is non-refundable — the rest comes back if the deal never happens: a posted job gets cancelled unfilled, or a service request is rejected, withdrawn, or superseded by another one. The posting or request form shows you the exact figure, and the total you are signing for, before you confirm. A posted job's amount cannot be edited afterwards, so changing the price means cancelling and posting again — and paying the fee a second time.
faq.a_wallets: MetaMask, Coinbase Wallet, Rainbow, Trust Wallet, Brave Wallet, OKX, Phantom, Ledger, and any injected wallet. WalletConnect lets you connect any mobile wallet.
faq.q_network: Which network does this run on?
faq.a_network: Currently deployed on Base Sepolia (testnet, chainId 84532). All USDC used is test USDC — no real money is at risk.
faq.q_get_usdc: How do I get test USDC?
faq.a_get_usdc: Use the Circle faucet at faucet.circle.com — select Base Sepolia and paste your wallet address. You'll receive test USDC within seconds. This is testnet only; no real money involved.
faq.a_how_deal:
1. Client creates a deal with executor address, amount, and deadline.
2. Client funds — USDC is locked in the contract.
3. Executor activates (accepts work).
4. Executor marks done.
5. Client releases payment — or raises a dispute.
6. If client is silent {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} after delivery, funds auto-release.
faq.q_no_activate: What happens if the executor doesn't activate?
faq.a_no_activate: If the executor doesn't activate within {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} after funding, the client can trigger a refund. Funds return to the client's wallet.
faq.q_deadline: What happens if the deadline passes?
faq.a_deadline: If the executor hasn't submitted work by the deadline, the client can trigger a timeout refund. Funds return to the client.
faq.a_cancel: The executor can decline before activating — the client can take a refund once the activation window of {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} has passed. Once active, there is no unilateral cancel; either party can raise a dispute instead.
faq.a_autoapprove: If the executor marks the work done and the client says nothing for {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}, the escrow is released to the executor. Once that window has passed anyone can trigger the release — the contract no longer needs the client to act. It stops a client from holding payment hostage.
faq.a_gasless: You sign a message with your wallet (no ETH needed). The platform relayer submits the transaction on-chain and pays the gas fee. Your wallet only signs — it does not spend ETH.
faq.q_safe_sign: Is it safe to sign gasless messages?
faq.a_safe_sign: Yes, with one caveat worth knowing. Each message is EIP-712 typed data bound to a specific contract, to the exact call (function and arguments) and to a one-time nonce, so the relayer can only forward your signed intent — it cannot alter the call, the target or the sender. What the envelope does not carry is an expiry: a request you signed but never sent stays valid until its nonce is used.
faq.a_censored: If the relayer is down, you can always call the contracts directly using any Ethereum wallet or tools like cast. Gasless is a convenience layer, not a requirement.
faq.q_raise_dispute: How do I raise a dispute?
faq.a_raise_dispute: On the deal page, tap 'Raise Dispute'. USDC is frozen immediately, and raising it already counts as your own answer. A registered arbiter can claim the case and review both sides. It also starts a clock for the other party: they have until the arbiter window closes to answer the dispute, and if nobody takes the case, whoever stayed silent gets only a quarter of the escrow.
faq.a_arbiters: Arbiters are addresses registered on-chain by the platform owner or chief arbiter. They are neutral third parties. At launch the roster is picked by hand: there is no open sign-up, and no date is set for one. You can view the full registry on the Arbiter page.
faq.q_claim: How does an arbiter claim a dispute?
faq.a_claim: Arbiters use a commit-reveal scheme: first commit a hash (to prevent front-running), then reveal in the next block to officially claim the deal. This ensures fair selection.
faq.q_outcomes: What are the possible dispute outcomes?
faq.a_outcomes: Four outcomes. Client wins: the escrow goes back to the client, minus the arbitration fee. Executor wins: the escrow goes to the executor, minus the same fee. Nobody takes the case in time and both sides answered the dispute: the escrow is split in half, and no fee is charged. Nobody takes the case and one side never answered: the silent side gets a quarter of the escrow, the rest goes to the side that answered — again no fee.
faq.q_arbiter_timeout: What if the arbiter doesn't resolve in time?
faq.a_arbiter_timeout: If no verdict lands within the arbiter window, either party can trigger an arbiter timeout. If an arbiter had taken the case, the whole escrow goes back to the client. If nobody ever took it, the outcome depends on who answered the dispute: both answered — the escrow is split in half, nobody judged, so nobody wins; one side stayed silent — that side gets a quarter and the rest goes to the side that answered.
faq.a_job_post: A client posts a job with description, budget, and requirements. Executors apply. The client selects one and a deal is created.
faq.a_service: An executor lists a service with a fixed price. Clients browse and request it directly, creating a deal.
faq.a_nft: Two different tokens, and neither is a reward for finishing. Posting a job mints a soulbound receipt for that posting to the client; it is burned when the client accepts an applicant or cancels the job. Funding a deal makes the Agreement itself mint one non-transferable token to the client and one to the executor — those stay for good, including after completion, as proof the deal existed. Reputation (XP) is separate and is awarded by the contract on completion.
faq.a_chat: Yes. Messages are encrypted end-to-end on your own devices — the server only stores unreadable data and holds no keys to it. There's no third-party messenger anymore, and no bot sitting inside your conversation. In a dispute, either side can present the conversation to the arbiter — from their own device; the platform can't hand it over from its own storage, because it can't read it either.
faq.q_files: Are files shared in chat private?
faq.a_files: Files are AES-256-GCM encrypted in your browser before upload, and the key stays inside the end-to-end encrypted conversation — the platform never holds it and can't decrypt the file. The server keeps the encrypted data only for a while: about 7 days from upload, longer while the deal stays open or a dispute is running, and never beyond 90 days — then it's deleted for good. In a dispute, you present the file yourself, from your own device; the platform has no readable copy to hand over.
faq.q_funds_safe: Can the platform take my funds?
faq.a_funds_safe: Not into its own pocket: an Agreement only ever pays the client, the executor, or the protocol's fee account for the arbitration fee, and its code cannot be changed after the deal is created. The honest limit is this — the platform owner can replace protocol facets and can overturn or freeze an arbiter's verdict before it becomes final, so a deal already in dispute can be decided by that key. The same key also gets past the treasury's own reserve gate, which our review measured at about 31,700 gas and wrote down in the repository; that is protocol money, not your escrow. So: it cannot take your escrow, but it can rule on it. That is a deliberate stage, not an oversight — testnet, test USDC, no external audit yet — and the plan is to move governance to a multisig at the mainnet launch, when real money is involved. Treat that as a stated plan, not as something the code enforces today.
faq.a_audited: The protocol is on Base Sepolia testnet and has not been formally audited. Do not use with significant real funds until a mainnet audit is completed.
faq.a_diamond: Diamond is an upgradeable proxy pattern where a single proxy contract delegates calls to multiple 'facet' contracts. This allows the protocol to be extended or fixed without redeploying everything.
faq.a_source: Available on GitHub — see the link on the page.
faq.q_verify: How do I verify the deployed contracts?
faq.a_verify: Inspect all contracts on BaseScan. Diamond address: {address}
faq.a_become_arbiter: Not for now. At launch the arbiter roster is picked by hand, and on-chain self-registration is switched off — applyAsArbiter() reverts for everyone, so the app does not offer you the button. Open entry is a later step and has no date. If you want to be considered, open an issue on GitHub.

footer.tagline: Decentralized freelance protocol on Base. The escrow logic runs on chain; governance is still one key, and the plan to hand it over is public.
